skill.description: Guide to using uv for fast Python dependency management, virtual environments, Python version pinning, locking, migration, and CI workflows.
skill.summary: Use uv to manage Python projects, dependencies, virtual environments, locks, and CI workflows.
skill.author: wshobson

security_audit.summary: Most external-command findings are Markdown code fences, not executable Ruby or shell backtick code. The audit confirms the remote installer patterns that pipe downloaded scripts into sh or PowerShell iex without verification. No prompt injection, credential theft, or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Replace curl piped to sh with a download, source review, and checksum or signature verification before execution.
Replace irm piped to iex with a documented download path and verification step before running the installer.
Tell users to replace placeholder repositories with trusted sources and review dependency provenance before installation.

content.value_statement: Python dependency workflows can be slow and inconsistent across local, CI, and Docker environments. This skill gives practical uv commands for projects, environments, locking, migration, and performance.
actual_capabilities: Shows installation options for uv on macOS, Linux, Windows, pip, Homebrew, and Cargo.
Explains project setup with uv init, uv add, uv sync, and uv lock.
Covers virtual environments, Python version pinning, and uv run workflows.
Provides migration paths from pip, pip-tools, Poetry, and requirements files.
Includes CI, Docker, monorepo, pre-commit, and VS Code examples.
Lists troubleshooting steps for PATH, Python versions, dependency conflicts, cache issues, and lockfiles.
limitations: It is documentation only; it does not install uv or run commands by itself.
Examples use placeholder repositories and packages that users must replace.
It does not verify remote installer scripts, package signatures, or repository trust.
uv features change quickly, so users should confirm behavior with official docs.

use_cases.title: Start a Python service
use_cases.description: Create a new uv project, pin Python, add runtime packages, and add test and lint dependencies.

use_cases.title: Modernize dependency workflows
use_cases.description: Move an existing requirements, pip-tools, or Poetry project toward uv commands and lockfile workflows.

use_cases.title: Speed up build pipelines
use_cases.description: Apply uv sync, frozen installs, caches, and Docker patterns to reduce CI setup time.

prompt_templates.title: Create a New Project
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a fresh Python project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the uv-package-manager skill to plan a new Python project named <project>. Include initialization, Python pinning, dependencies, dev tools, and the first test run.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate Existing Dependencies
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate migration from pip or Poetry.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the uv-package-manager skill to migrate this project to uv. Explain how to handle requirements files, pyproject.toml, lockfiles, and developer setup.

prompt_templates.title: Improve CI Reliability
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the uv-package-manager skill to design a CI dependency workflow. Include frozen installs, Python setup, cache strategy, test commands, and failure checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Monorepo Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workspace planning for multiple packages.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the uv-package-manager skill to propose a uv workspace for a Python monorepo. Cover member layout, shared dependencies, local packages, lockfiles, and developer commands.

output_examples.input: Plan a uv setup for a new FastAPI service with tests and linting.
output: A step-by-step setup sequence for the project directory and Python version.
A dependency plan that separates runtime packages from test and lint tools.
A short verification checklist for running the app, tests, and formatting checks.

output_examples.input: Help migrate a requirements-based project to uv.
output: A migration path that preserves existing dependency constraints.
Guidance on creating a lockfile and updating contributor instructions.
Compatibility notes for teams that still need requirements exports.

output_examples.input: Review my CI dependency installation strategy.
output: Recommendations for frozen installs and cache reuse.
A pipeline outline that installs Python, syncs dependencies, and runs checks.
Risk notes about stale locks, cache misses, and unreviewed dependency updates.

best_practices: Commit uv.lock and use frozen installs in CI for reproducible builds.
Pin the Python version so local and automated environments use the same interpreter.
Use uv run for commands so tools execute inside the managed project environment.
anti_patterns: Running remote installer scripts without reviewing source, checksums, or signatures.
Mixing manual virtual environment activation with uv run in the same workflow.
Updating dependencies without reviewing lockfile changes and compatibility impact.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps plan uv commands for Python projects, dependencies, virtual environments, locks, migration, and CI.

faq.question: Does the skill run uv commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and command examples for users or agents to review before running.

faq.question: Can it replace pip or Poetry workflows?
faq.answer: It explains migration paths from pip, pip-tools, Poetry, and requirements files to uv workflows.

faq.question: Does it support Docker and CI?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for Docker builds, GitHub Actions, frozen installs, and cache reuse.

faq.question: What should I check before using install commands?
faq.answer: Review the source, prefer signed releases, and avoid piping downloaded scripts directly into a shell.

faq.question: Is this skill specific to Claude Code?
faq.answer: No. It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
